mainTopic: Who keeps the כתובה in forbidden marriages, and the cases where the two reasons split; then a new משנה on when engagement, pregnancy, or waiting for a יבם affects eating תרומה and מעשר
overview: The amud finishes a ברייתא about why some forbidden marriages still come with a כתובה and others do not. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says it depends on whether the couple becomes disqualified. רבי says Torah bans need no extra penalty, while rabbinic bans like שניות do. A third reason, 'who encourages whom', is credited either to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר or to רבי, who added it because of the case of a חלוצה. The גמרא then looks for a case where these reasons give different results. It tries a ממזרת married to a regular Jew, a man who remarries his ex-wife after she married someone else, a בעולה married to a כהן גדול, and a ספק סוטה. Each case is rejected by some תנא's view that the marriage would harm her or her children. The case that finally holds up is a definite סוטה. A new משנה then teaches that engagement, pregnancy, or waiting for a יבם can take away a woman's right to eat תרומה or מעשר but can never give it. The גמרא asks why מעשר is mentioned at all, and answers that the משנה follows רבי מאיר, who forbids מעשר ראשון to non-Levites. The ברייתא that proves this comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Who gets penalized: the disqualified couple versus the fit couple
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר finishes his rule. When both husband and wife become disqualified, the husband is penalized and must pay the כתובה. In the case of שניות, where both stay fit, the wife is penalized and loses her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They penalized him with the כתובה. And why did they say that שניות forbidden by rabbinic law get no כתובה? Because he is fit and she is fit, and wherever he is fit and she is fit, they penalized her with the כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is finishing the words of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. It explains why the forbidden-to-a-כהן cases get a כתובה while the שניות cases do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a marriage like an אלמנה to a כהן גדול, both spouses become disqualified (פסול), so the couple has a strong reason to divorce. Here the rabbis penalize the husband by making him pay. In שניות nobody becomes disqualified, so there is no natural push to divorce, and the rabbis penalize the wife by taking away her כתובה so that she will want to leave.

keyTerms.meaning: They (the rabbis) penalized
The marriage contract payment owed to a wife at divorce or widowhood
Secondary relatives, forbidden only by rabbinic law
Rabbinic law
Fit, not disqualified (for כהונה)

steps.confusionAlert: 'They penalized him' means he still has to pay the כתובה. 'They penalized her' means she loses it.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: If both spouses are disqualified, the husband is penalized and pays the כתובה. If both stay fit (שניות), the wife is penalized and gets no כתובה.

steps.title: Torah bans need no reinforcement, rabbinic bans do
steps.stepSummary: רבי gives a different reason. The כהן cases are Torah prohibitions, which do not need extra rabbinic reinforcement. שניות are rabbinic, so the rabbis strengthened them by taking away the כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: These are Torah law, and Torah law needs no strengthening. Those are rabbinic law, and rabbinic law needs strengthening.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי disagrees about the reason. For him, the question is whether the ban comes from the Torah or from the rabbis.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People already take Torah bans seriously, so no extra penalty is needed and the woman keeps her כתובה. People might take a rabbinic ban lightly, so the rabbis added a penalty (no כתובה) to make sure it is kept.

keyTerms.meaning: Torah law
Strengthening, reinforcement
These / those

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a general principle used in many places: rabbinic laws sometimes get extra safeguards that Torah laws do not need.

phrases.english: Rabbi says:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה.

phrases.english: These are Torah law,

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah prohibitions keep the כתובה because they need no reinforcement. Rabbinic prohibitions lose it as a reinforcement.

steps.title: A third reason: who encourages whom
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא offers another explanation. In the disqualified case the husband talks her into the marriage, so he is penalized. In the שניות case she talks him into it, so she is penalized.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: In this case he encourages her, and in that case she encourages him.
steps.whatsHappening: A third reason is given. The rabbis penalize whichever spouse is likely pushing the forbidden marriage forward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the marriage disqualifies her, she has more to lose, so he is probably the one pushing it, and he must pay. When nobody is disqualified, she has little to lose and is probably the one pushing, so she loses the כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: Another explanation
He entices or encourages her
She entices or encourages him

phrases.english: Another explanation: In this case, he encourages her,
phrases.notes: 'This case' is the couple who become disqualified, like the אלמנה with a כהן גדול.

phrases.english: and in that case, she encourages him.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The spouse who likely pushes the forbidden marriage is the one penalized.

steps.title: Whose opinion is the third reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא taught the 'another explanation'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who teaches the 'another explanation'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who said the third reason. This sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not say whose words 'another explanation' are. It could belong to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר or to רבי, and the answer changes how we understand it.

steps.title: First answer: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר explaining his own rule
steps.stepSummary: Some say רבי שמעון בן אלעזר taught it. He is giving the reason behind his own rule about disqualified and fit couples.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רבי שמעון בן אלעזר teaches it, and he is explaining the reason. Why did they say that when he is disqualified and she is disqualified they penalized him? Because he encourages her. And why, when he is fit and she is fit, did they penalize her? Because she encourages him.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer says the third reason is not a new opinion at all. It is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר explaining why his own rule works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this view, 'another explanation' really means 'what is the reason?'. Being disqualified or fit is the case, and 'who encourages whom' is the reason behind each penalty.

steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רבי teaches it, and the case of a חלוצה was a difficulty for him:

steps.deeperAnalysis: On this view, 'another explanation' is a later addition by רבי to his own Torah-versus-rabbinic rule. The next step shows what forced him to add it.

steps.title: A חלוצה is forbidden only by the rabbis, yet she gets a כתובה
steps.stepSummary: A חלוצה married to a כהן is forbidden only by rabbinic law, yet she still gets her כתובה. That goes against רבי's rule that rabbinic bans need reinforcement.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a חלוצה is forbidden by rabbinic law, and she does have a כתובה!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the challenge to רבי's rule. A rabbinic ban should have lost the כתובה, but in the case of חלוצה it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי said rabbinic bans are reinforced by taking away the כתובה. A חלוצה with a כהן is a rabbinic ban where the כתובה is still paid, so his rule cannot be the whole story.

keyTerms.meaning: By rabbinic law
And she does have

phrases.english: But a ḥalutza is forbidden by rabbinic law,
phrases.notes: He means forbidden to a כהן.

phrases.english: and she does have a marriage contract!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא חֲלוּצָה דְּרַבָּנַן וְאִית לַהּ כְּתוּבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the difficulty mentioned in the previous step
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's rule that rabbinic prohibitions lose the כתובה as reinforcement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חלוצה is a rabbinic prohibition, yet the כתובה is not taken away

steps.title: רבי adds: since the marriage disqualifies her, he is the one encouraging
steps.stepSummary: רבי answers that the marriage to a כהן disqualifies the חלוצה, even if only rabbinically. So the husband is the one pushing the marriage, and he is penalized. In שניות, nobody is disqualified, so she pushes it and is penalized.
steps.simpleTranslation: He then said: Since he disqualifies her by rabbinic law, in this case he encourages her, and in that case she encourages him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי fixes his rule by adding the 'who encourages whom' reason. This explains why a חלוצה keeps her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deciding factor is no longer just Torah versus rabbinic law. It also matters whether the marriage disqualifies her. A חלוצה becomes disqualified, so the husband is penalized and she keeps the כתובה. In שניות no one is disqualified, so she loses it.

keyTerms.meaning: He then said, he went back and said
Since
He disqualifies her

steps.whatToRemember: The 'he encourages her / she encourages him' reason is either רבי שמעון בן אלעזר explaining his own rule, or רבי's addition to answer the problem raised by חלוצה. Either way, whoever likely pushes the forbidden marriage is the one penalized.

phrases.english: He then said:
Since he disqualifies her by rabbinic law,
in this case, he encourages her,
and in that case, she encourages him.
phrases.notes: 'That case' is the שניות, where neither of them becomes disqualified.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר: כֵּיוָן דְּפָסֵיל לָהּ מִדְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from חלוצה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a second reason alongside the original principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every rabbinic prohibition should lose the כתובה
steps.terutzMaskana: When the marriage disqualifies her, even rabbinically, he is the one encouraging it, so he pays and she keeps the כתובה

steps.title: What is the practical difference between the two opinions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between רבי and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between רבי and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks in which case the two reasons we just learned would give different results. This question sets up the attempts that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One reason says the woman gets her כתובה because her marriage is forbidden by the Torah, and Torah bans need no extra rabbinic penalty. The other reason says it depends on who is pushing for the marriage. In the usual cases both reasons give the same answer, so the גמרא looks for a case where they split.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them? It asks for a case where the two views give different results.

phrases.english: What is there between Rabbi
and Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar?
phrases.notes: He means: in what practical case would their two reasons give different answers?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין רַבִּי לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting out both reasons, the גמרא asks where they lead to different outcomes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the Torah-law reason and the 'who is pushing' reason give different answers about the כתובה.

steps.title: רב חסדא: a ממזרת or נתינה married to a Jew
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the difference is a ממזרת or נתינה married to a regular Jew. By the Torah-law reason she gets her כתובה. By the 'who is pushing' reason she pushes, so she loses it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The difference is a ממזרת or a נתינה married to a Jew. The one who says it depends on Torah law says this is also Torah law, so she gets her כתובה. The one who says it is 'because he encourages her' says that here she encourages him, so she does not get it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא offers a case where the two reasons split: a ממזרת or נתינה married to a regular Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This marriage is forbidden by the Torah, so the Torah-law reason says no rabbinic penalty is needed and she gets her כתובה. The other reason looks at who is pushing. She is already disqualified no matter what, and marrying a regular Jew gives her descendants a path to become fit (a ממזר son of hers could marry a maidservant, and their children could be freed). So she is the one pushing, and she is penalized.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman born from a forbidden union such as עריות, who may not marry a regular Jew
A woman descended from the גבעונים, who may not marry a regular Jew
Forbidden by Torah law
He encourages her / she encourages him, meaning who is pushing for the marriage

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
A mamzeret or a Gibeonite woman married to a Jew
is the difference between them.
According to the one who says it depends on Torah law,
this too is Torah law,
phrases.notes: So no extra rabbinic penalty is needed, and she gets her כתובה.

phrases.english: according to the one who says it is because he encourages her,
here she encourages him.
phrases.notes: She is the one pushing for the marriage, so she is penalized and loses her כתובה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מַמְזֶרֶת וּנְתִינָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ממזרת or נתינה married to a regular Jew: by the Torah-law reason she gets her כתובה, and by the 'pushing' reason she does not.

steps.title: According to רבי אליעזר she gains nothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that according to רבי אליעזר, a ממזר's child from a maidservant stays a ממזר. So the ממזרת gains nothing from the marriage and would not be pushing for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי אליעזר, who said the child is both a slave and a ממזר, she does not encourage him at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא's case. It says his explanation of why she would push for the marriage does not work according to רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her reason to push for this marriage was the hope that her descendants could one day become fit. According to רבי אליעזר, a ממזר's child from a maidservant is still a ממזר, so that hope is gone. Then she has no special reason to push, and רב חסדא's case is not a clear difference for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: A slave and a ממזר, so his lineage can never become fit
Not at all

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Eliezer, who said
"this one is a slave and a mamzer,"
phrases.notes: He is talking about the child of a ממזר and a maidservant. For רבי אליעזר that child can never become fit.

phrases.english: she does not encourage him at all!

steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that a ממזרת is the one pushing for the marriage
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Her reason to push depends on her descendants being able to become fit. רבי אליעזר rejects that, so according to him she has no reason to push.

steps.title: רב יוסף: remarrying a divorcée after she married someone else
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the difference is a man who remarries his ex-wife after she was married to another man. By the Torah-law reason she gets her כתובה. By the 'who is pushing' reason she pushes, so she loses it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: The difference is one who remarries his divorcée after she married someone else. The one who says it depends on Torah law says this is also Torah law. The one who says it is 'because he encourages her' says that here she encourages him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא's case was rejected, so רב יוסף suggests a new case where the two reasons split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Remarrying your ex-wife after she married someone else is a Torah ban, so by the Torah-law reason she gets her כתובה. By the other reason, the marriage costs her nothing, since she is not disqualified and her children are not affected. That makes her the one pushing, so she is penalized.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who remarries his divorced wife after she was married to someone else, which the Torah forbids

steps.title: According to רבי עקיבא her children would be ממזרים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that according to רבי עקיבא, children from a union forbidden by a לאו are ממזרים. So this marriage would harm her, and she would not be the one pushing for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי עקיבא, who said a child from a union forbidden by a לאו is a ממזר, she does not encourage him at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף's case. It says the case does not work according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף assumed the marriage costs her nothing. But remarrying a divorcée after she married someone else is a לאו, and רבי עקיבא holds that children from such a union are ממזרים. So she loses a lot by this marriage, and she would not be the one pushing for it.

steps.title: רב פפא: a בעולה married to a כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the difference is a בעולה, a woman who is not a virgin, married to a כהן גדול. By the Torah-law reason she gets her כתובה. By the 'who is pushing' reason she pushes, so she loses it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: The difference is a בעולה married to a כהן גדול. The one who says it depends on Torah law says this is also Torah law. The one who says it is 'because he encourages her' says that here she encourages him.
steps.whatsHappening: Both earlier cases were rejected, so רב פפא offers a third case, a בעולה married to a כהן גדול. The next step challenges this case too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן גדול marrying a בעולה goes against the Torah, so by the Torah-law reason she gets her כתובה. This ban is only a positive commandment, not a לאו, so even רבי עקיבא would not call her children ממזרים. The marriage costs her nothing, so she is the one pushing, and by the second reason she is penalized.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is not a virgin
The High Priest, whom the Torah commands to marry a virgin

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:
a non-virgin married to a High Priest
is the difference between them.
According to the one who says it depends on Torah law,
this too is Torah law,
and according to the one who says it is because he encourages her,
here she encourages him.
phrases.notes: This ban is a positive commandment, not a לאו, so her children are fine even according to רבי עקיבא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בְּעוּלָה לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב יוסף's rejected case with one that stands up even according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A בעולה married to a כהן גדול: by the Torah-law reason she gets her כתובה, and by the 'pushing' reason she does not.

steps.title: Challenge to רב פפא from רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, a child from a union forbidden by a positive commandment with a כהן is a חלל. So the בעולה would lose something and would not be the one pushing for the marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who says a child from a union forbidden by a positive commandment is a חלל, she gains nothing here and would not be pushing him at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב פפא's case of a בעולה married to a כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's case only works if the woman loses nothing by the marriage, because then she is the one pushing for it. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds that her children would be חללים, so the marriage does harm her. That means she has no reason to push, and the 'who is pushing' reason would not take away her כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: A child of a כהן from a forbidden union, who loses the status of כהונה
Unions forbidden by a positive commandment
She encourages him, meaning she is the one pushing for the marriage

phrases.english: But according to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who said
there is a חלל from unions forbidden by a positive commandment,

phrases.aramaic: הָא לָא מַרְגְּלָא לֵיהּ וְלָא מִידֵּי!
phrases.english: then she does not encourage him at all!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's proposed case from step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's case of a בעולה married to a כהן גדול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If her children become חללים, the marriage harms her, so she is not the one pushing for it. Then the two reasons would agree after all.

steps.title: רב אשי: a husband who takes back a ספק סוטה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the difference is a man who takes back a wife who may be a סוטה. Living with her is forbidden by the Torah, but it does not harm her or her children, so she is the one pushing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: the difference between them is a man who takes back a wife who might be a סוטה. The one who says 'it is Torah law' says this too is Torah law, so she gets her כתובה. The one who says 'because he encourages her' says that here she encourages him, so she loses it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a new case where the two reasons give different answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A possible סוטה is forbidden to her husband by the Torah. So by the Torah-law reason, no extra penalty is needed and she keeps her כתובה. But staying married does not damage her status or her children, so she is the one pushing for it, and by the 'who is pushing' reason she loses her כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: A wife who was warned and then secluded with another man, so it is unclear whether she sinned
Takes back, meaning keeps living with her
There is a difference between them
From Torah law

phrases.english: Rather, רב אשי said:
One who takes back his wife who might be a סוטה is the difference between them.
According to the one who says it is because it is Torah law,
this too is Torah law,
phrases.notes: So no extra penalty is needed, and she keeps her כתובה.

phrases.english: and according to the one who says it is because he encourages her,
here she encourages him.
phrases.notes: So she is the one at fault, and she loses her כתובה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב פפא's rejected case with a new one
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A husband who takes back a ספק סוטה. It is forbidden by Torah law, and the woman loses nothing, so she is the one pushing.

steps.title: Challenge to רב אשי from רבי מתיא בן חרש
steps.stepSummary: רבי מתיא בן חרש holds that a husband who has relations with a ספק סוטה even on the way to the test makes her a זונה. So she is harmed and would not push.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי מתיא בן חרש, who says that even if her husband was on his way to make her drink the test water and had relations with her on the way, he made her a זונה, she gains nothing here and would not be pushing him at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב אשי's case using the view of רבי מתיא בן חרש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If living with a ספק סוטה makes her a זונה, she becomes forbidden to marry a כהן. So the marriage does harm her, and she has no reason to push for it. Then the 'who is pushing' reason would not take away her כתובה either.

keyTerms.meaning: To make her drink the bitter test water of a סוטה
A woman who is forbidden to marry a כהן because of a forbidden relationship

phrases.english: But according to רבי מתיא בן חרש, who said:
even if her husband went to make her drink the test water,
and had relations with her on the way,
he has made her a זונה,

phrases.aramaic: הָא לָא מַרְגְּלָא לֵיהּ וְלָא מִידֵּי!
phrases.english: then she does not encourage him at all!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי מַתְיָא בֶּן חָרָשׁ, דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's case from step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's case of a husband who takes back a ספק סוטה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If living with her makes her a זונה, the marriage harms her, so she would not be the one pushing.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי: a definite סוטה
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי says the difference is a definite סוטה. Living with her is forbidden by the Torah, and she has nothing more to lose, so she is the one pushing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, מר בר רב אשי said: the difference between them is a definite סוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי gives the final case where the two reasons give different answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wife known for sure to have sinned is forbidden to her husband by the Torah. So by the Torah-law reason she keeps her כתובה. Staying with her husband adds no new harm to her or her children, so even רבי מתיא בן חרש would agree she is the one pushing, and by that reason she loses it.

keyTerms.meaning: A wife who definitely sinned with another man

steps.whatToRemember: The final case where the two reasons give different answers is a definite סוטה. Living with her is forbidden by the Torah, but it adds no new harm to her, so she is the one pushing.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rather, מר בר רב אשי said:
A definite סוטה is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב אשי's rejected case with a case that holds up even according to רבי מתיא בן חרש
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A definite סוטה. It is forbidden by Torah law, and living with her husband adds no new harm to her, so she is the one pushing.

steps.title: New משנה: engagement, pregnancy or waiting for a יבם does not give the right to eat
steps.stepSummary: An Israelite woman engaged to, pregnant from, or waiting for a יבם who is a כהן may not eat תרומה. If the man is a לוי, she may not eat מעשר. The same situations take away a כהן's or לוי's daughter's right when the man is an Israelite.
steps.simpleTranslation: An Israelite woman who is engaged to a כהן, pregnant from a כהן, or waiting for a יבם who is a כהן, and likewise a כהן's daughter in these situations with an Israelite, may not eat תרומה. An Israelite woman who is engaged to a לוי, pregnant from a לוי, or waiting for a יבם who is a לוי, and likewise a לוי's daughter in these situations with an Israelite, may not eat מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists situations that are not enough to give a woman the right to eat holy food, but are enough to take that right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Engagement, pregnancy from a man who died, and waiting for a יבם do not count as full marriage for giving an Israelite woman the right to eat תרומה or מעשר. But for a כהן's or לוי's daughter, these same situations with an Israelite already take away the right she had in her father's house. So these situations can take away a right, but cannot give one.

keyTerms.meaning: Engaged (betrothed) but not yet fully married
Pregnant (here, from a husband who died)
A widow waiting for her husband's brother to do יבום or חליצה
The holy portion of produce given to a כהן
The tithe of produce given to a לוי

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'similarly' (וכן) flips the case. It means the daughter of a כהן or לוי who is in one of these situations with an Israelite man. She loses her right to eat.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
An Israelite woman engaged to a כהן,
pregnant from a כהן,
waiting for a יבם who is a כהן,
and likewise a כהן's daughter with an Israelite —
phrases.notes: He means a כהן's daughter who is engaged to, pregnant from, or waiting for a יבם who is an Israelite.

phrases.english: may not eat תרומה.
An Israelite woman engaged to a לוי,
pregnant from a לוי,
waiting for a יבם who is a לוי,
and likewise a לוי's daughter with an Israelite —
may not eat מעשר.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל מְאוֹרֶסֶת לְכֹהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the previous discussion is finished
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Engagement, pregnancy, or waiting for a יבם does not let a woman eat תרומה or מעשר through the man, but these situations do take away a כהן's or לוי's daughter's right when the man is an Israelite.

steps.title: A לוי's daughter with a כהן, and a כהן's daughter with a לוי, eat neither
steps.stepSummary: A לוי's daughter engaged to, pregnant from, or waiting for a יבם who is a כהן, and a כהן's daughter in these situations with a לוי, may eat neither תרומה nor מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: A לוי's daughter who is engaged to a כהן, pregnant from a כהן, or waiting for a יבם who is a כהן, and likewise a כהן's daughter in these situations with a לוי, may eat neither תרומה nor מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes with a mixed case where both rules from the last step apply at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A לוי's daughter with a כהן does not gain תרומה, because these situations cannot give a right. She also loses the מעשר she ate in her father's house, because they do take a right away. The same is true in the reverse case of a כהן's daughter with a לוי, so in both cases she ends up eating neither.

keyTerms.meaning: The daughter of a לוי
Neither תרומה nor מעשר

steps.whatToRemember: These three situations (engagement, pregnancy, waiting for a יבם) can only take away a right to eat holy food. They never give one. That is why the mixed cases end up eating nothing.

phrases.english: A לוי's daughter engaged to a כהן,
pregnant from a כהן,
waiting for a יבם who is a כהן,
and likewise a כהן's daughter with a לוי —

phrases.aramaic: לֹא תֹאכַל לֹא בִּתְרוּמָה וְלֹא בְּמַעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.english: may eat neither תרומה nor מעשר.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּת לֵוִי מְאוֹרֶסֶת לְכֹהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies both rules of step 19 together in a mixed case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the mixed cases she loses her father's right and does not gain the man's, so she eats neither תרומה nor מעשר.

steps.title: Why Mention מעשר? Even a Non-Levite May Eat It
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling that an Israelite woman engaged to a לוי may not eat מעשר. A non-Levite may eat מעשר anyway, so what is the משנה adding?
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: Let her simply be a non-Levite. Doesn't a non-Levite woman also eat מעשר?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and immediately questions the משנה. Why would an Israelite woman engaged to a לוי be barred from מעשר, when any non-Levite may eat it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike תרומה, מעשר has no special holiness that limits who may eat it. It is just the לוי's property, and he can give it to anyone. So treating her as a plain זרה should change nothing, and the משנה's ruling seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that follows and explains the משנה
Here: a woman who is not from the tribe of לוי
Tithe, the tenth of the produce given to a לוי
Doesn't she...? A question that expects the answer 'of course she does'

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse מעשר with תרומה. תרומה is holy and only כהנים and their households may eat it. That is exactly why the גמרא is surprised that מעשר would be restricted.

phrases.english: GEMARA: And let her be a non-Levite!
Does a non-Levite woman not eat מעשר?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְהֵא זָרָה, זָרָה מִי לָא אָכְלָה בְּמַעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by challenging the משנה's ruling in step 19 about מעשר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that an Israelite woman engaged to, pregnant from, or waiting for a יבם who is a לוי may not eat מעשר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Non-Levites are allowed to eat מעשר. Losing a right that even outsiders have makes no sense, so the ruling seems to have no meaning.

steps.title: The משנה Follows רבי מאיר: מעשר ראשון Is Forbidden to Non-Levites
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting שמואל, answers that the משנה follows רבי מאיר, who holds that מעשר ראשון is forbidden to non-Levites. The גמרא then introduces a ברייתא as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: Whose view is this? It is רבי מאיר, who said that מעשר ראשון is forbidden to non-Levites. As it is taught in a ברייתא:
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the question by saying the משנה follows רבי מאיר's opinion. The last word, דתניא, sets up a ברייתא that the גמרא will quote next as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that non-Levites may eat מעשר. רב נחמן says that is not everyone's view: according to רבי מאיר, מעשר ראשון may not be eaten by non-Levites. So the משנה's ruling does mean something. Because she is not a לויה, she cannot eat it.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this? A way of naming the author of a teaching
First tithe, the tenth of the produce given to a לוי
Here: people who are not from the tribe of לוי

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the משנה's ruling about מעשר depends on a disagreement. It follows only the view that restricts מעשר ראשון to Levites.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Shmuel said:
Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Meir,
who said: First tithe is forbidden to non-Levites.
As it is taught in a baraita:

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מַנִּי — רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 21 by naming רבי מאיר as the author of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the משנה to a specific תנא (רבי מאיר) whose view supports its ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed everyone agrees that non-Levites may eat מעשר, so the משנה's ruling seemed meaningless.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי מאיר, who forbids מעשר ראשון to non-Levites. So an Israelite woman who is not yet married to the לוי cannot eat it.
